blocks.text: תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית.

אֲדוֹן עוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר מָלַךְ. בְּטֶרֶם כָּל־יְצִיר נִבְרָא:
לְעֵת נַעֲשָׂה בְחֶפְצוֹ כֹּל. אֲזַי מֶלֶךְ שְׁמוֹ נִקְרָא:
וְאַחֲרֵי כִּכְלוֹת הַכֹּל. לְבַדּוֹ יִמְלוֹךְ נוֹרָא:
וְהוּא הָיָה וְהוּא הֹוֶה. וְהוּא יִהְיֶה בְּתִפְאָרָה:
וְהוּא אֶחָד וְאֵין שֵׁנִי לְהַמְשִׁיל לוֹ לְהַחְבִּירָה:
בְּלִי רֵאשִׁית בְּלִי תַכְלִית. וְלוֹ הָעֹז וְהַמִּשְׂרָה:
וְהוּא אֵלִי וְחַי גֹּאֲלִי. וְצוּר חֶבְלִי בְּעֵת צָרָה:
וְהוּא נִסִּי וּמָנוֹס לִי. מְנָת כּוֹסִי בְּיוֹם אֶקְרָא:
בְּיָדוֹ אַפְקִיד רוּחִי. בְּעֵת אִישַׁן וְאָעִירָה:
וְעִם־רוּחִי גְּוִיָּתִי. יְיָ לִי וְלֹא אִירָא:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ עַל נְטִילַת יָדָיִם:

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר יָצַר אֶת־הָאָדָם בְּחָכְמָה וּבָרָא בוֹ נְקָבִים נְקָבִים חֲלוּלִים חֲלוּלִים. גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לִפְנֵי כִסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ שֶׁאִם יִפָּתֵחַ אֶחָד מֵהֶם אוֹ יִסָּתֵם אֶחָד מֵהֶם אִי אֶפְשַׁר לְהִתְקַיֵּם וְלַעֲמוֹד לְפָנֶיךָ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ רוֹפֵא כָל־בָּשָׂר וּמַפְלִיא לַעֲשׂוֹת:
In most communities of the German rite אלהי נשמה (P. 5.) follows here.
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ לַעֲסוֹק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה:

uncertainties: Holam-male dots on vav are often faint at this resolution. In line 1, אדון/עולם may lack a visible holam dot. I wrote the full spelling (אֲדוֹן עוֹלָם) and have not confirmed it.

Asher yatsar, line 3: I could not confirm at this resolution that both doublings are printed (נְקָבִים נְקָבִים חֲלוּלִים חֲלוּלִים). One of the repeated words might be missing. Check this against a higher-resolution scan.
Final kaf with qamats in כְבוֹדֶךָ and לְפָנֶיךָ: the qamats looks present but small.
Adon Olam line 5 has no medial period. I kept it that way, since that is how the other lines would show a caesura.
The Divine Name is printed as יְיָ throughout.
Running head: the period after שַׁחֲרִית is visible on this page.
Page number 4 appears in both corners. I recorded it once as the printed label.

blocks.text: Morning Prayer

אדון Lord of the world, He who has reigned before any form was created.
At the time when by His will everything came into being, then was His Name proclaimed as King.
And after everything ceases to be then He alone inspiring awe will reign.
He was, He is and He will be in glory.
He is unique and there is no second to compare with Him or to associate with Him.
Without beginning, without end, to Him might and dominion belong.
He is my God and my Redeemer lives .
The rock of my portion in time of distress.
He is my banner and a refuge for me, the portion of my cup on the day I call.
Into His hand I entrust my spirit at the time I sleep and I awake.
And with my spirit my body.
God is with me, I do not fear.
ברוך Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has sanctified us through His commandments and commanded us to wash the hands.

ברוך Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who with wisdom formed man and created in him many openings, many cavities. It is manifest and known before the throne of Thy glory that if one of them were to remain open or one of them to remain closed, it would be impossible to exist and to appear before Thee. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who heals all flesh and works wonderfully.
In most communities of the German rite אלהי נשמה (P. 5.) follows here.
ברוך Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has sanctified us through His commandments and commanded us to occupy ourselves with the words of the Torah.

uncertainties: Line-end hyphens are joined: 'in-spiring' became 'inspiring' and 'com-manded' became 'commanded' (twice).
There is a stray dot above the hyphen in 'in-' at the end of the 'And after everything' line. It looks like a printing speck.
Each Adon Olam line starts its own indented paragraph. I separated them with newlines.

blocks.text: תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית

וְהַעֲרֶב־נָא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֶת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָתְךָ בְּפִינוּ וּבְפִי עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִהְיֶה אֲנַחְנוּ וְצֶאֱצָאֵינוּ וְצֶאֱצָאֵי עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל כֻּלָּנוּ יוֹדְעֵי שְׁמֶךָ וְלוֹמְדֵי תוֹרָתֶךָ (לִשְׁמָהּ). בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַמְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר־בָּנוּ מִכָּל־הָעַמִּים וְנָתַן לָנוּ אֶת תּוֹרָתוֹ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ נוֹתֵן הַתּוֹרָה:

יְבָרֶכְךָ יְיָ וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ: יָאֵר יְיָ פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וִיחֻנֶּךָּ:
יִשָּׂא יְיָ פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וְיָשֵׂם לְךָ שָׁלוֹם:

אֵלּוּ דְבָרִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שִׁעוּר הַפֵּאָה וְהַבִּכּוּרִים וְהָרְאָיוֹן וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים וְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה: אֵלּוּ דְבָרִים שֶׁאָדָם אוֹכֵל פֵּרוֹתֵיהֶם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְהַקֶּרֶן קַיֶּמֶת לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן כִּבּוּד אָב וָאֵם וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים וְהַשְׁכָּמַת בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ שַׁחֲרִית וְעַרְבִית וְהַכְנָסַת אוֹרְחִים וּבִקּוּר חוֹלִים וְהַכְנָסַת כַּלָּה וְהַלְוָיַת הַמֵּת וְעִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה וַהֲבָאַת שָׁלוֹם בֵּין אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ וְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה כְּנֶגֶד כֻּלָּם:

אֱלֹהַי נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה (הִיא) אַתָּה בְרָאתָהּ אַתָּה יְצַרְתָּהּ אַתָּה נְפַחְתָּהּ בִּי וְאַתָּה מְשַׁמְּרָהּ בְּקִרְבִּי וְאַתָּה עָתִיד לִטְּלָהּ מִמֶּנִּי וּלְהַחֲזִירָהּ בִּי לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא: כָּל־זְמַן שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה בְקִרְבִּי מוֹדֶה אֲנִי לְפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהַי וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתַי רִבּוֹן כָּל־הַמַּעֲשִׂים אֲדוֹן כָּל־הַנְּשָׁמוֹת. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַמַּחֲזִיר נְשָׁמוֹת לִפְגָרִים מֵתִים:

uncertainties: (לִשְׁמָהּ) and (הִיא) are printed in smaller type inside parentheses. I kept them inline.
Mappiq in לִשְׁמָהּ, בְרָאתָהּ, יְצַרְתָּהּ, נְפַחְתָּהּ, מְשַׁמְּרָהּ, לִטְּלָהּ and וּלְהַחֲזִירָהּ: the dots look present but are hard to confirm at this resolution.
וִיחֻנֶּךָּ is written with a dagesh in the final kaf, which is the standard Masoretic form. I did not confirm it at the pixel level.
Dagesh and qubbuts in כִּבּוּד: I read כִּבּוּד, but the first dagesh is faint.
בְקִרְבִּי appears twice. The first (after מְשַׁמְּרָהּ) looks like בְּקִרְבִּי with a dagesh. The second (after שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה) looks like בְקִרְבִּי without one. Both readings are uncertain.
The Priestly Blessing is set as two centred lines, and I kept that split.
Running head: no period is visible after שַׁחֲרִית, unlike p. 4.
Page number 5 appears in both corners.

blocks.text: Morning Prayer

והערב And so, O Lord our God, let the words of Thy Torah be pleasing in our mouth and in the mouth of Thy people the House of Israel so that we and our descendants and the descendants of Thy people the House of Israel may all acknowledge Thy Name and learn Thy Torah (with pure intent). Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who teaches the Torah to His people Israel .
ברוך Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has chosen us from all peoples and given us His Torah. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the giver of the Torah.
יברכך May the Lord bless you and protect you. May the Lord cause His countenance to shine on you and be gracious to you. May the Lord raise His countenance towards you and grant you peace.

אלו The following matters have no legal measure:
The corner of the field, the first fruits, the pilgrimage, the practice of charity and study of the Torah. With regard to the following matters man receives an income in this world and the capital is stored for him in the future world: honouring father and mother the practice of charity, early attendance in the House of Study mornings and evenings, hospitality towards strangers, care of the sick, endowment of a bride, escorting the dead, concentration during prayer, peace making between man and his fellow man with the study of Torah outweighing all of them.

אלהי My God, the soul which Thou hast given me is pure. Thou didst create it, Thou didst form it, Thou didst breathe it into me and preserve it within me. Thou wilt eventually take it from me and restore it to me in the future world. As long as the soul is within me I thank Thee, O Lord my God, and God of my fathers, Lord of all works, Master of all souls. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who returns souls to dead bodies.

uncertainties: Line-end hyphens are joined: 'hon-ouring', 'atten-dance' and 'hospital-ity'.
In the 'אלו' paragraph, 'The corner of the field' starts a new line with no indent. I kept it as a line break within one block.

notes: I read only the four images. I did not consult any transcription, OCR or other evidence.

Possible source issue on s44: I could not confirm the doubled נְקָבִים נְקָבִים חֲלוּלִים חֲלוּלִים. If only one doubling is printed, it is a source variant or error. Verify this at higher resolution.
Apparent typesetting quirks on s45: a space before the period in 'my Redeemer lives .', and a stray dot above 'in-'.
Apparent typesetting quirks on s47: a space before the period in 'His people Israel .', and no comma between 'honouring father and mother' and 'the practice of charity'.
s44 and s45 both have the instruction 'In most communities of the German rite אלהי נשמה (P. 5.) follows here.', which points to the Elohai Neshamah text on printed page 5 (s46).
On the English pages, a Hebrew cue word starts each paragraph: אדון, ברוך, והערב, יברכך, אלו, אלהי. I kept each one at the start of its block text.

The pointing was read from images shown at about 88% scale. Small marks (holam-male dots, mappiq, dagesh, meteg) are the least certain parts of this transcription. I noted no metegs because none were clearly visible.
